full_judgment:
6. Mr Enayetur Rahim for opposite party No. 1, submits that the case was filed by making an application under section 14(2) of the Act for direction upon the umpire to file the award in Court for making the same a Rule of the Court and a judgment thereupon and the application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code for rejecting such application is totally misconceived. Defending the decision of the learned Subordinate Judge, he also submits that the petitioner earlier made an application for setting aside the award. In the case, opposite party No. 1 applied for making the award a Rule of the Court. Then, the petitioner withdrew the case. Opposite party No. 1 was then constrained to make the application under section 14(2) of the Act within time of such withdrawal. In the circumstances, the learned Subordinate Judge was therefore; right to hold that no decision on the question of limitation could be given without evidence. 

 7. In the revision application it is stated that the petitioner filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1997 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge at Dhaka for setting aside the award dated 15-10-96. The case was on transfer to the Court of Additional Subordinate Judge at Dhaka renumbered as Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1997. Opposite party No. 1 appeared and opposed the application by filing a written objection. It also made an application under section 14(2) of the Act for making the award a Rule of the Court and for judgment under section 17 of the Act. On 4-5-99 the petitioner withdrew the Miscellaneous Case. Then, on 4-8-99 opposite party No. 1 made a fresh application under section 14(2) for making the award a Rule of the Court and for a judgment under section 17 of the Act. The application was registered as a title suit. How such application could be registered as a suit, we fail to comprehend. However, such numbering would not make such application a plaint. Because, what a plaint should contain has been provided by Order VII rule 1 of the Code. In the cause title of the application, we find provision of section 14(2) is invoked, and relief is prayed for under section 17 of the Act. Order VII rule 11 of the Code has provided the incidents and circumstances when a plaint would be liable to be rejected. In the circumstances, the application made under section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act is not a plaint. The application of the petitioner under Order VII rule 11 of the Code for rejection of such application is wholly misconceived and is, therefore, not maintainable. 

 8. Moreover, on the question of limitation, the law is very clear. Article 178 of the Limitation Act has provided for a period of ninety days for filing in Court of the award. Such period will only commence from the date of service of notice of making the award. We could not find any date when such notice, if any, was at all issued or served. Such issue on limitation could only be properly raised and decided in the hearing of the case. In the circumstances, we do not find any reason to take a view different from that of the learned Subordinate Judge. The impugned order therefore does not suffer from any error or illegality or results in failure of justice.
